note: CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) SOURCE, level 1: the item wording and the response anchors come from the study's own deposited codebook -- sheet 'Sheet1' of S1 Data (PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0237710.s001, xlsx, sha256 fa2b99f0d23219d36d5da5b1325813dc512b412d2ee21f25d8cbb7e63c3bd951), which is a two-column 'Variable name / Variable label' codebook. Row 336 carries the block header 'Knowledge of Complications ', rows 337/341/345/349/353/357/361 carry kc1_kidney..kc7_circulation with their full sentences, and each is followed by its three value labels '1 Yes' / '2 No' / '3 Don’t know'. The IRW codes ARE the data sheet's own column headers (data/afaya_2020_diabetes_ghana.py melts the kc* columns unrenamed via pandas.melt, no positional assignment), so mapping_basis=data_labels: code -> text is tied at the source, at both the variable-label and value-label level. Codebook rows for kc2/kc4/kc6 carry a trailing space in the variable name ('kc2_feeling '); that is a spreadsheet artifact and was stripped -- the codes shipped are the data sheet's exact headers, which validate_items.R confirms against the live set. (2) STEP 3b -- right subscale: the deposit's knowledge battery is 66 items in seven labelled blocks (gk 11, kd 13, km 7, ke 4, kom 10, kf 14, kc 7); the seven live items are exactly the kc block sitting under the codebook's own 'Knowledge of Complications' header, so these are the complications items and not the diet/exercise/footcare blocks queued for other rounds. (3) INSTRUMENT-NAME DISCREPANCY, real and disclosed: the paper's Methods says 'the 23 item diabetes knowledge test questionnaire (DKT) developed by scholars from the University of Michigan was used' [refs 26,27], but the deposit administers 66 knowledge items across seven subscales. Some wording is recognisably Michigan DKT/DKN lineage ('Diabetes often causes poor circulation', 'Cuts and abrasions on diabetes heal more slowly' in the gk block), but the battery as administered is larger than and not identical to the published DKT-23, so `instrument` names the study's own questionnaire rather than asserting DKT-23. (4) VERIFICATION NOT WRITTEN: mapping_basis is data_labels and the derivation is pattern 1 (the code IS the source column name), so Step 5b is exempt and no verification row or verify_<table>.R is owed. Corroborating read anyway, not relied on: kc3_vision and kc6_hyposexual are the block's two negatively-worded items and kc6 carries the highest mean (2.05) and the lowest floor% (27.0) of the seven, which is what a 'No is correct' item looks like on a 1=Yes/2=No/3=Don’t know coding. (5) LANGUAGE: participants qualified if they 'could speak, read, and write in English or Dagbani' and the English instruments were forward- and back-translated into Dagbani, so the administration was bilingual; language='English; Dagbani' per the semicolon-list rule. The base fields hold the ENGLISH version, which is a genuinely administered version and the study's own material -- not a substitute -- so text_source= study_materials and translation_source is blank. The Dagbani wording appears nowhere in the deposit or the article's Supporting Information (S1 Data is the only supplement) and was not hunted off-source. (6) correct_response is BLANK for all seven. The paper says 'Every question had three answer choices with only one correct answer', but neither the codebook nor the article states which; a key here would be IRW adjudicating medical fact, not transcription, so it was left empty and key_source is blank. (7) instructions and section_prompt are blank -- the codebook and the article publish no administration instructions for the knowledge battery; section_id is the single trivial afaya_2020_complications_knowledge_1. (8) RIGHTS: no reserved right locatable. IRW's wording is copied from the study's own CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE deposit. On the upstream instrument, the Michigan Diabetes Research Center distributes its survey instruments free of charge with an attribution condition only -- 'By downloading the forms, users are agreeing to acknowledge the MDRC as the source of the items in the survey instruments in any written instruments, reports, or publications resulting from their use or reproduction' (medresearch.umich.edu/survey-instruments). That is a CC-BY-shaped attribution requirement; it reserves no fee, no NC, no ND and no permission gate, and it expressly contemplates reproduction, so it does not block. The live page 403s automated fetches and web.archive.org was down at the time of this round, so that sentence is quoted from a search-engine extract of the page rather than a fetched copy with a hash -- flagged so a later reader can re-verify. No register row was written (a round may write `block` but never `ship`). (9) RETRY TEST: NO for the shipped table -- it passed and an unchanged retry would produce the same file. The two open items are determinate, not access failures: the Dagbani wording is not published anywhere in scope, and the answer key was never published by the study. A direct fetch of the MDRC terms page (currently bot-walled) would only firm up an already non-blocking clause.
public_note: Item wording and the Yes / No / Don’t know anchors are transcribed verbatim from the study's own deposited codebook (S1 Data), and the item codes are that file's own column headers, so the code-to-text mapping is tied at the source. Two caveats. The paper's Methods describes a 23-item Michigan Diabetes Knowledge Test, but the deposited questionnaire is a 66-item battery in seven labelled blocks, of which these seven are the 'Knowledge of Complications' block -- so the instrument is the study's own questionnaire rather than the published DKT-23. And although every question has one correct answer, neither the paper nor the codebook says which, so correct_response is left blank rather than asserted by IRW. The questionnaire was administered in English or Dagbani depending on the participant; the English version ships here and the Dagbani form is not published in the deposit.

source_ref: Wesselmann ED, Ispas D, Olson MD, Swerdlik ME, Caudle NM (2018) Does perceived ostracism contribute to mental health concerns among veterans who have been deployed? PLOS ONE 13(12): e0208438, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0208438 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 File .sav (journal.pone.0208438.s001, sha256 07e302954b6c74d7c7c5be6a8253fe65720a53fc5d7b9333e4f403eda8cd2b33) variable labels for ost1-ost10; authors' codebook https://osf.io/enp9g/download 'Military-ostracism-archived-codebook.pdf' (sha256 b3e1ee71d817f05ec4902a6321cbaa9498537a31041dfa135059152acc358a9c), section 'Chronic Ostracism (Carter-Sowell, 2010)', for the instructions and the three printed anchors; instrument is the Ostracism Experience Scale for Adults (Carter-Sowell AR, dissertation, Purdue University, 2010; cf. Gilman et al., Psychol Assess 2013;25:319-330)
note: Ground truth: 10 items (ost1..ost10), resp 1-7, 1,246 rows. TEXT/MAPPING: item_text is the 10 SPSS variable labels of ost1-ost10 in the PLOS S1 File, transcribed character for character, and the authors' OSF codebook lists the same 10 codes against the same 10 sentences with 10/10 exact string equality after curly-quote normalisation -- an independent corroboration of both the wording and the code-to-text tie. No label is near the 255-char SPSS cap (longest, ost2, is 102 chars), so no truncation. ost3's label reads 'In general, others treatment as if I am invisible.' -- a grammatical error present identically in BOTH study sources; shipped as administered rather than normalised to 'treat me as if'. CODE DERIVATION: data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts value_vars=[f'ost{i}' for i in range(1,11)], so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- derivation pattern 1, no rename and no positional step, hence Step 5b exempt (data_labels) and no verify_<table>.R. The .sav's own per-item non-missing n reproduces the live table exactly for all ten items (125,125,125,125,124,125,125,122,125,125) and so do the per-item resp maxima (7,6,6,7,6,7,6,7,7,7), which is a further check that these ten columns are what IRW shipped. STEP 3b: passes. The paper's Measures section describes ten items answered 'using a 7-point scale (1-Hardly Ever; 7-Almost Always)' with Cronbach's alpha = .96, and quotes two items verbatim -- 'In general, I feel ignored' (ost9) and 'In general, others treat me as if I'm in solitary confinement' (ost6); the .sav's other scales sit under their own prefixes (drri*, social*, pcl*, trait*, state*, need*, dis*, msp*), so 'ostracism' names the right instrument. SCALE DIRECTION, checked against the data (N=125 in the .sav): the file's own 'chronic ostracism average' composite equals the UNREVERSED mean of ost1..ost10 exactly (max |diff| = 0.000; the reversed mean is off by up to 6.000), and that composite correlates +0.649 with the ptsd composite, +0.627 with distress, +0.611 with traitanx, -0.550 with social support and -0.781 with basic-need satisfaction, so a HIGH value means MORE ostracism: 1 = Hardly ever, 7 = Almost always, exactly as codebook and paper print. All ten items are positively keyed (minimum inter-item r = +0.598, no reverse items and no *R columns for this scale), and raw-item alpha = 0.963 reproduces the paper's .96. DEVIATIONS: option_text is populated only at resp=1 ('Hardly ever'), resp=4 ('Some of the time') and resp=7 ('Almost always'), the three anchors the codebook prints; resp 2,3,5,6 are left BLANK because the .sav carries no value labels at all (variable_value_labels is empty) and neither study source labels the intermediate points -- they were not padded with their own numbers. instructions is the codebook's own Chronic Ostracism prompt, quoted with its enclosing curly quotes stripped and the line wrapping joined; nothing else was changed. section_prompt is blank and section_id is the single trivial wesselmann_2018_ostracism_1 (no testlets). correct_response is blank throughout (no correct answer). RIGHTS: no block, and none of the standing exclusions apply. The wording IRW copied came from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit's own variable labels plus the authors' own OSF codebook. The originator is Carter-Sowell (2010), a Purdue dissertation; there is no instrument page, no register row in instrument_rights_register.csv, and no quotable clause from the rights holder reserving a fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution right could be located (checked 2026-09-20: APA PsycTests doiLanding 10.1037/t29695-000 returns a JS shell with no terms; the two third-party aggregator pages that surface the scale, statistics.datanalysis.net/questionnaires/aggression/oes-8/ and psychologyroots.com/ostracism-experience-scale-oes/, state nothing from the rights holder -- the latter's 'you must obtain permission directly from the author' line is Psychology Roots' own disclaimer about itself, and it is in any case attached to a DIFFERENT scale, Shahzad et al.'s Pakistani OES). Silence is permission, so extracted normally; no register row written (a round may write block rows only). RETRY TEST: not applicable, the table passed.

source_ref: Wesselmann ED, Ispas D, Olson MD, Swerdlik ME, Caudle NM (2018) Does perceived ostracism contribute to mental health concerns among veterans who have been deployed? PLOS ONE 13(12): e0208438, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0208438 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 File .sav (journal.pone.0208438.s001, sha256 07e302954b6c74d7c7c5be6a8253fe65720a53fc5d7b9333e4f403eda8cd2b33) variable labels for social1-social15; authors' codebook https://osf.io/enp9g/download (sha256 b3e1ee71d817f05ec4902a6321cbaa9498537a31041dfa135059152acc358a9c), section 'Civilian-Based Social Support (DRRI; King, King, & Vogt, 2003)', for the instructions and the rating-scale line; response anchors corroborated by the paper's Measures section ('1-Strongly Disagree, 5-Strongly Agree'). Instrument: Deployment Risk and Resilience Inventory (DRRI) Postdeployment Social Support Scale (King DW, King LA, Vogt DS, 2003); NCPTSD page https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/deployment/postdeployment-support.asp (sha256 7f1ce8b7bbcee0d8dbccdc112670cd827689f92f45039802027b4a7ee8ed5feb, read 2026-09-20). IRW processing script: data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py.
note: item_text = the 15 SPSS variable labels of social1-social15 in the PLOS S1 File, transcribed verbatim (label lengths 57-100 chars, far under the 255 SPSS truncation cap, so no label is a prefix). The authors' OSF codebook lists the same 15 codes against the same 15 sentences -- checked programmatically, 15/15 identical after collapsing the codebook's PDF line wrapping. Code derivation is pattern 1: data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts value_vars=[f'social{i}' for i in range(1,16)], so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- no rename, no positional step, hence Step 5b exempt and no verify_<table>.R. instructions = the codebook's own prompt for this scale, transcribed verbatim including its typo 'after your most recently deployment' (not normalised); the enclosing curly quotation marks that delimit it in the codebook were dropped. option_text = the codebook's own [Rating Scale: ...] line, with ONE correction: the codebook prints position 1 as 'Strongly Agree', which duplicates position 5 and is the same misprint this codebook makes for the DRRI Deployment Concerns scale; the paper's Measures section states '1-Strongly Disagree, 5-Strongly Agree' and the NCPTSD scale page states 5-point Likert (1 = "Strongly disagree" to 5 = "Strongly agree"), so position 1 ships as 'Strongly Disagree'. The other four labels are the codebook's own wording and casing. No anchor is padded with its own number. Direction verified on the data (N=128, no inference left unchecked): social6R and social8R equal 6-social6 and 6-social8 exactly (max |diff| = 0.0), and the file's own 'support' composite equals mean(social1-5, social6R, social7, social8R, social9-15) with max |diff| = 0.000 against max |diff| = 0.533 for the plain raw mean -- so the IRW table stores social6 and social8 RAW (unreversed) and higher raw = more support on the 13 positively-worded items. That composite correlates -0.511 ptsd, -0.461 traitanx, -0.393 stateanx, -0.532 distress, -0.550 chronic ostracism, +0.594 basicneeds, +0.596 milsupport, fixing 5 = Strongly Agree; the -0.550 reproduces the paper's reported civilian-support x ostracism r = -.55, and keyed alpha 0.902 (n=124) reproduces the paper's reported .90. Item content agrees: the two negatively-worded items social6 (2.85) and social8 (3.48) are the two lowest means of 15. Step 3b: the paper names the Post Deployment Social Support subscale of the original DRRI (King, King & Vogt 2003), 15 items, 1-5 -- which is what the live data is (15 items, resp 1-5). NOT the DRRI-2, whose revised Section O 'Postdeployment Support' is a 10-item rewrite; that form was read and rejected as the wording source. What this does NOT establish: nothing tests the three interior anchors individually; only the endpoints and the monotone direction are checked against data. Rights: no block. NCPTSD 'To Obtain Scale' -- "This measure was created by staff at VA's National Center for PTSD." with free direct downloads; the only qualifier, "These measures are intended for use by qualified mental health professionals and researchers.", disclaims fitness and reserves no right (the LOT-R shape). No register row written -- a DRRI ship_with_note row is flagged for Ben rather than self-written, as in batch_270.
